objections: Rare-category merge with minGroup=5 is close to a no-op here: of 32 distinct names only the two singletons (the _ldap SRV lookup and upload.nimbusdrive.example) fall below 5, so srk.example (66, religious body, Art. 9), liitto.example (100, union), ajanvaraus.terveyspalvelu.example and apteekki.example (health) and tyopaikat.example (job search) all survive verbatim.

Combined with the consistent client_hostname/client_ip pseudonyms, the MSSP analyst gets a per-employee profile of union, religious, health and job-search lookups, which is exactly the browsing disclosure the threat model names and is disproportionate under Finnish working-life privacy law.

It also coarsens in the wrong direction for security: the singletons it merges (an LDAP SRV recon-style lookup and an upload domain) are the more security-relevant rows, while sensitive high-volume names stay.

A dataset-scoped keyed token keeps per-domain frequency, beaconing and cross-table consistency for correlation without exposing names; no listed utility task (U1-U11) depends on DNS name lexical content.
